title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 84-87): Grothendieck wants a workable description of how Γ = Gal(K̄/K) acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid π̂_1(X; I), where X is a K-variety and I is a finite set of K-rational base points. The previous page notes that describing the action through one base point x_0, chosen paths l_i from x_0 to x_i, and generators λ_j works in principle (data (42)-(43)). But it depends on arbitrary choices. It is especially unsuitable when a finite symmetry group 𝔊 acts on X and I is 𝔊-stable. The top of this page gives the reason: one can practically never find a K-rational point x ∈ X_K fixed by 𝔊. So one must work with groupoids on 𝔊-stable sets of several base points rather than with a single base point.

Before giving his method for 'symmetric' computations, he first reduces the Γ-action on π̂_1(X; I) to the Γ-action on π̂_1(U_{0,3}) = π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}).

Hypotheses: K is a number field and X is smooth, quasi-projective and geometrically connected over K.

Claim (44): using Lefschetz-type theorems together with Belyi's theorem, one 'should be able' to find K-morphisms I ⊂ C → X and f: C → U_{0,3} with the following properties.
- C is a smooth curve over K containing I.
- i: C → X induces a surjection on fundamental groups.
- f is finite étale (completed on p. 87).

Modern reading of the steps:
1. Lefschetz/Bertini. A general complete-intersection curve section of X through the finite set I, defined over K, gives π_1(C) ↠ π_1(X). Hence there is a full surjective functor of groupoids π̂_1(C; I) ↠ π̂_1(X; I), and it is Γ-equivariant.
2. Belyi. C̄ has a K-morphism to P^1 unramified outside {0,1,∞}. Shrinking C to the preimage of U_{0,3} makes f finite étale, and surjectivity onto π_1(X) is preserved.
3. Groupoid coverings (p. 87). Put I_0 = f(I) ⊂ U_{0,3}(K) and I' = f^{-1}(I_0) ⊃ I. Then π̂_1(C; I) is a full subgroupoid of π̂_1(C; I'), which is a finite covering of π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0).

Conclusion: for any such X over a number field, the Galois action on π̂_1(X; I) is determined by the action of an open subgroup of G_Q on the 'universal' object π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0). Here I_0 is a finite set of genuine K-rational (not tangential) base points.

This is the groupoid, multi-base-point, higher-dimensional version of the principle behind the faithfulness of G_Q on π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points) and the 'universality' of U_{0,3} later stressed in the Esquisse.
errors: Gap: f must be finite étale onto U_{0,3}, so the points of I must avoid f^{-1}{0,1,∞}. Belyi's theorem as usually stated does not guarantee that a prescribed finite set of points avoids the fibres over 0, 1, ∞. Grothendieck hedges with 'doit pouvoir'. This needs a strengthened Belyi lemma, or tangential base points, or a modified choice of C.

Lefschetz with base points: one needs a curve section that passes through the prescribed points I, is defined over K, and still has π_1(C) → π_1(X) surjective. This is plausible (Bertini/Goresky–MacPherson/Deligne-type results in characteristic 0) but is not justified on the page.
On p. 87 the transcription has π_1(X, I) 'appearing as a subgroup' of π_1(C, I). Since i is surjective, it is a quotient; this is probably a transcription or wording issue.

ideas.what: No 𝔊-fixed K-rational point exists in practice, so symmetric computations need groupoids on a 𝔊-stable set of base points.
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with several (symmetry-stable) base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); groupoids in topology from R. Brown
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2-3 (Teichmüller groupoids, base points stable under symmetries)

ideas.what: Lefschetz + Belyi: every smooth quasi-projective X over a number field receives a curve C with π_1(C) ↠ π_1(X) and C finite étale over P^1 − {0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Belyi's theorem combined with Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (1979), Lefschetz/Bertini–Goresky–MacPherson; consequences for Galois actions: Ihara, Matsumoto, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions Belyi and faithfulness on π̂_1(P^1−3pts); the higher-dimensional Lefschetz reduction is not stated there to my knowledge

ideas.what: The Galois action on π̂_1(X; I) is determined by the action on π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0), I_0 a finite set of K-rational points, via finite groupoid coverings and full subgroupoids.
ideas.modern_name: universality of π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) for Galois actions; Galois action on path torsors between rational points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi/Ihara (faithfulness); Wojtkowiak, Nakamura for paths between rational points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse states the universal role of U_{0,3} loosely

missed.claim: An explicit reduction of the Galois action on profinite fundamental groupoids of arbitrary smooth quasi-projective varieties over number fields, with arbitrary finite sets of K-rational base points, to the action on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with K-rational (not tangential) base points. It combines Lefschetz-type surjectivity, Belyi, and groupoid coverings. The literature mostly treats curves, outer actions or tangential base points; the multi-point, higher-dimensional groupoid formulation is rarely stated.
missed.quote: Utilisant des th. du type Lefschetz, plus le résultat de Белый, on doit pouvoir trouver des homomorphismes de schémas sur K  I ⊂ C →i X, f: C → U_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It ties anabelian/Galois-action computations for higher-dimensional varieties to ℓ-adic polylogarithms and path torsors between rational points on P^1−3 points (Wojtkowiak, Nakamura). It also motivates a 'Belyi avoiding prescribed points' lemma.

missed.claim: The needed strengthening of Belyi (a Belyi map on C for which the prescribed K-points of I lie outside the fibres over 0, 1, ∞) is assumed without proof.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small but genuine lemma needed to work with honest rational base points instead of tangential ones.

deep.surprise_reason: The Belyi-universality idea is well known and in spirit in the Esquisse. The explicit higher-dimensional Lefschetz + Belyi reduction for groupoids with several rational base points, motivated by symmetry groups without rational fixed points, is a nice unpublished detail but not a major surprise.
transcription_corrections: Diagram (44): I ⊂ C sits atop a vertical arrow f: C → U_{0,3}, with i: C → X horizontal.
'Biel' is struck out and replaced by Cyrillic 'Белый' (Belyi), consistent with a date after 1979.
'des homomorphismes [?] de schémas' should read 'des homomorphismes de schémas'.
The marginal insertion before 'Je prendrai' reads 'et'; the phrase 'dans l'optique des opérations de Γ' is an insertion on the crossed-out line.
